children: By by Jack Denton and Janet H. Cho
Spotify Technology stock jumped Thursday as the wider stock market fell after the streaming platform reported more premium subscribers than it had previously forecast.
More importantly: profit growth is ahead of estimates as it looks like investments into AI are bearing fruit. It's a reminder that chip stocks and their ilk aren't the only winners from the AI trend.

Spotify stock was up 10.5%, to $580.48 in mid-afternoon trading on Thursday after the company posted quarterly results. The S&P 500 index was down 1.5%, dragged lower by technology stocks and especially the chip sector.

Spotify reported revenue of 4.97 billion euros ($5.58 billion) in the September quarter, up 16% from a year ago but ever-so-slightly missing estimates of EUR4.98 billion among analysts surveyed by FactSet. Earnings per share came in at EUR2.48.

Premium revenue rose 17%, driven by higher subscribers and average revenue per user, while advertising-supported revenue grew 10%. Gross margin of 33% and operating income of EUR672 million both came in above guidance.

What looks especially good: Spotify said its premium subscriber base grew to 306 million in the last quarter, a million more paying customers than it had previously guided. Of that figure, 36% came from Europe, 25% from North America, 24% from Latin America, and 15% from the rest of the world.
Monthly active users increased 11% to 788 million, and ad-supported monthly active users grew 12% to 499 million.

"When we went public in 2018, we had 71 million subscribers. Since then, every single year we've been adding 25 million subs or more," with a goal to reach 315 million subscribers by the end of the year, co-CEO Alex Norström told analysts. "Through the pandemic, price increases, and a changing economy and consumer landscape, this steady growth in subscribers hasn't stopped. And this quarter, that growth came from every region."

In its forecast for the current fourth quarter, Spotify sees revenue at EUR5.2 billion ($5.84 billion), with a 33.8% gross margin. It expects to add another 10 million premium subscribers, to 316 million, and increase its monthly active users to 818 million.
Even better: Spotify expects operating income of EUR820 million ($920 million) in the current quarter, firmly ahead of analysts' expectations.

It looks like the AI thesis for Spotify is finally playing out. Significant investments into AI — such as the platform's AI DJ feature, which curates music for listeners — have raised spending fears among investors.

Operating income in the third quarter came in at EUR672 million, with margins squeezed slightly from earlier in the year, partly reflecting the growth in expenses "driven by temporarily elevated growth in marketing and cloud/AI spend," the company said.
Operating income forecast to jump to EUR820 million should ease some of those spending fears — and drive optimism among investors that AI bets are paying off.

Spotify is also integrating with Meta Platforms' AI agent Muse to let listeners ask their agent to play music, save songs to their library, build personalized playlists, and find new books and podcosts.
"On our fourth-quarter call back in February, I said that we were building the world's first truly intelligent agentic media platform," co-CEO Stig Gustav Victor Söderström said.
"We made a bet that consumers using services like ChatGPT would also start demanding intelligence from their media service. So, we build for that."

He said Spotify is "unusually well-positioned for the age of agentic AI," because unlike most companies, Spotify can "monetize from the background," noting that it has been in the background of apps like Waze and Google Maps for decades.

"This was a quarter where we did what we said. We've built a strong business that keeps compounding, we invest when we see a path for growth, our costs are moderating, and there's more runway ahead," Norström said in a statement. "Every time we expand what's on Spotify, we bring in new listeners and give existing ones more reasons to come back, almost every day."

To keep subscribers coming back, Spotify is expanding its audiobooks to more than 180 markets by the end of 2026, from 22 markets previously. Users will gain access to more than 350,000 titles in 120 languages, including Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, and Polish.
While Spotify stock has lagged in 2026 — the shares are down 1.9% so far this year — some analysts have seen the streaming platform as highly defensible against AI.
As the stock market grapples with weakness on Thursday driven by AI concerns, while Spotify outperforms, there is added symbolism to that thesis.
